(1) patents are an important source of scientific knowledge, (2) patents are a valuable resource to extract facts that are not available in the biomedical literature, (3) the extraction of such facts is a challenging task, and (4) there is much potential to further improve the extraction of facts from patents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic identification and extraction of biomedical facts from patent documents.
extracting knowledge from patents and making this knowledge accessible for the biomedical research community.
developing text mining methods that are able to identify and extract biomedical entities and facts from patents.

the field has not reached maturity yet and that there are still a lot of challenges to overcome.
there is still a need for more work in this area.
the text mining of patents for biomedical knowledge has not reached the level that it has for the literature.

the patent mining has been a very active area of research in the past decade.
the patent literature is an under-exploited resource for biomedical research and drug development.
we have provided the first systematic review of the state of the art in text mining of biomedical patents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
text mining patents is a highly promising area that has not yet been fully exploited.
the mining of biomedical knowledge from patents is an exciting area of research that has the potential to make a significant contribution to the biomedical research community.
